title: Ossuary
description:
Ossuary shows you the numbers you would otherwise have to remember.

[b]Deck tracker[/b] — what is left in your draw pile, grouped, with the chance of drawing each card next turn. The draw count is read from the game, so relics and powers that change how much you draw are already accounted for. When the pile is shorter than your draw, the cards coming back from the reshuffle get their own section at real odds.

[b]Incoming damage[/b] — what every enemy intends, hit counts included, what it costs after block, and a clear warning when the turn would kill you. The numbers come from the game's own damage calculation, so strength, vulnerable and weak are already applied.

[b]Tier ratings on offers[/b] — community grade, score, win rate and pick rate on the cards, relics and potions you are offered.

[b]About the ratings[/b]
Ossuary uses Spire Codex community data, but re-bands it. Codex's published tiers put 30% of cards in F and 26% in D — more than half the game in the bottom two grades, which makes the list useless for choosing between two cards. Ossuary places the same scores on a normal curve instead. Ratings are bundled with each release and refreshed per build; the mod makes no network requests while you play.

[b]It reads and displays only[/b]
Ossuary changes no rule, pool, price or outcome, and declares affects_gameplay: false. It is still a mod, so runs played with it loaded are flagged as modded by the game's own reporting. If that matters to you, don't install it.

[b]Controls[/b]
F9 hides and shows the HUD. F10 enters layout mode, where panels can be dragged and - and + resize the text. Everything is saved between sessions.

[b]Credits[/b]
Community data by Spire Codex (spire-codex.com). Modelled on Reliquary by Brandon Barker. Unofficial and not affiliated with Mega Crit or Spire Codex.

Source: https://github.com/christofferbraun/ossuary
